## What the data says
- Thin fabric: no PSI test data at 30 % O₂, 70.3 kPa; physics estimate shows adiabatic flame temperature ≈ 2550 K, 220 K above the hottest tested thin-fabric condition (~2320 K) [PSI-68] [PSI-69]
- Thin solid: no PSI test data at 30 % O₂, 70.3 kPa; physics estimate shows adiabatic flame temperature ≈ 2550 K, 220 K above the hottest tested thin-solid condition (~2330 K) [PSI-68] [PSI-69]
- Thick solid: no PSI test data at 30 % O₂, 70.3 kPa; physics estimate shows adiabatic flame temperature ≈ 2550 K, 220 K above the hottest tested thick-solid condition (~2330 K) [PSI-68] [PSI-69]
- Liquid fuel droplets (methanol, n-heptane): 8 methanol droplet runs at 30-34 % O₂, 71.2-72.1 kPa, 0 cm/s flow all sustained; 100 % evidence coverage 0.892 [PSI-69]
- Fire-resistant materials (silicone, Nomex): 8 runs at ≤ 22.2 % O₂; 3 kept burning, 5 did not (3 Nomex, 0 silicone) [PSI-25] [PSI-99]

## How confident we can be
- Solid data: 131 of 134 ordinary solid runs sustained; only 2 extinction-velocity limits and 1 no-ignition run, so flammability limits cannot be located [PSI-25] [PSI-98][PSI-99]
- Thin-fabric, thin-solid, thick-solid: no test data at target conditions; confidence limited to physics estimates only [PSI-68] [PSI-69]
- Droplet data: high evidence coverage (0.892) and all nearby runs sustained, giving strong support for sustained combustion at 30 % O₂ [PSI-69]
- Fire-resistant materials: mixed results; 3 of 8 sustained, indicating potential for burning at ≤ 22.2 % O₂ [PSI-25] [PSI-99]

## Gaps
- No PSI microgravity test data for thin fabric, thin solid, or thick solid at 30 % O₂, 70.3 kPa; physics estimates only [PSI-68] [PSI-69]
- Partial-gravity combustion data missing; microgravity and Earth-gravity results do not bound lunar or Martian gravity, which may be more hazardous (Ferkul et al., LPSC 2026, NTRS 20260000646)
- Fire-resistant materials tested only up to 22.2 % O₂; no data at 30 % O₂ (NTRS 20070018178)

## What future experiments (e.g. LUCI, FM2) should measure
- Thin-fabric, thin-solid, and thick-solid combustion at 30 % O₂, 70.3 kPa, 0 cm/s flow in microgravity to locate flammability limits
- Partial-gravity (≈ 0.38 g) combustion tests for all material classes to assess whether flame spread thresholds shift relative to 1-g and microgravity
- Fire-resistant material tests at 30 % O₂, 70.3 kPa to determine if Nomex HT90-40 or silicone sustain burning under Martian-like conditions (NTRS 20070018178)
- Droplet combustion with varied flow rates to evaluate the influence of ventilation on sustained burning at Martian oxygen levels
- High-pressure, high-oxygen tests for thin fabrics to confirm physics estimates and refine adiabatic flame temperature margins.
